claim: When a coarse maximum sits at the top end of its span, dino-autofocus's focus search lays out the next span centred at the old top with a half-width equal to the old span's full width, swept upward from its low end so that z never jumps upward, and stops extending when the ceiling leaves nothing above the old top; a maximum at the low end is reported as re-centre lower.
validity_conditions: Describes the order and layout of spans only. Every span size, centre, floor and ceiling is an argument the caller supplies, and in this repository the floor and ceiling come from the person's per-objective focus limits, not from dino-autofocus. The drafted sentence also said the operator is asked before each extension and that extensions are bounded in number; that half is DISCARDED as a procedure of dino-autofocus's own engine, and the count as a figure -- whether and how often to extend is the 11-24 design's and the person's. 10.2.1: TRANSFER. Place: a store entry -- the one place 10.2's 2026-10-03 paragraph opens for dino-autofocus before 11-24 designs the focus search, so that design can cite the method without any code having crossed. Rule: 10.3 rule 1, capped at E3 as a run taken in another project. No figure crosses (rules 3 and 4): every threshold the method uses is its caller's argument and none is entered. It says what the method IS at the pinned commit, not that it works on this stand.

valid_until.no_event: The claim describes one file at one commit, identified by its LF-normalised body sha256, so nothing ends it. A later change to that file in dino-autofocus is a new source, and the entry describing it supersedes this one.
